title: Provider map: Event-driven processing
body:
**aws**: SQS queue with dead-letter queue + AWS Lambda + DynamoDB
**azure**: Azure Storage Queues with poison queue + Azure Functions + Table Storage
**gcp**: Pub/Sub topic with dead-letter topic + Cloud Functions + Firestore

title: Event-driven processing on AWS
body:
SQS queue with dead-letter queue + AWS Lambda + DynamoDB

**Plan only**: `terraform/aws/event-driven`

**Watch out**: The event source mapping and redrive policy reference ARNs; verify both resolve in the plan without live state.

title: Event-driven processing on AZURE
body:
Azure Storage Queues with poison queue + Azure Functions + Table Storage

**Plan only**: `terraform/azure/event-driven`

**Watch out**: Storage Queue and Table names must be lowercase, and Function App names are globally unique.

title: Event-driven processing on GCP
body:
Pub/Sub topic with dead-letter topic + Cloud Functions + Firestore

**Plan only**: `terraform/gcp/event-driven`

**Watch out**: Dead-letter policies need a topic id and delivery attempt count; keep the trigger and subscription on the same project.

title: Q1: What does a dead-letter destination provide in an event-driv
body:
A. It caches successful responses for faster reads
B. It isolates messages that repeatedly fail processing
C. It replaces the queue when traffic spikes
D. It encrypts the topic at rest

**B.** A dead-letter queue or topic captures poison messages after a retry limit so the main stream keeps flowing.

title: Q2: Which combination models the event-driven pattern across all
body:
A. Queue or topic, consumer function, and dead-letter or storage
B. API gateway, function, and relational database
C. Load balancer, virtual machine, and block storage
D. CDN, static files, and DNS record

**A.** Each provider fixture names a queue or topic, a function to consume events, and a dead-letter destination plus state storage.

title: Provider map: Serverless API
body:
**aws**: API Gateway HTTP API + AWS Lambda + DynamoDB
**azure**: API Management + Azure Functions + Table Storage
**gcp**: Cloud Run endpoint + Cloud Functions + Firestore

title: Serverless API on AWS
body:
API Gateway HTTP API + AWS Lambda + DynamoDB

**Plan only**: `terraform/aws/serverless-api`

**Watch out**: Lambda invoke permissions and integration URIs are easy to miswire; check the API Gateway source ARN in the plan.

title: Serverless API on AZURE
body:
API Management + Azure Functions + Table Storage

**Plan only**: `terraform/azure/serverless-api`

**Watch out**: Function App and Storage Account names are globally unique, and API Management needs publisher details even in a plan.

title: Serverless API on GCP
body:
Cloud Run endpoint + Cloud Functions + Firestore

**Plan only**: `terraform/gcp/serverless-api`

**Watch out**: Cloud Functions needs a runtime, entry point, and source location at plan time; supply placeholders, never credentials.

title: Q1: What is the provider-neutral core of the serverless API patt
body:
A. A long-running VM behind a load balancer
B. An HTTP endpoint, a stateless function, and a managed store
C. A message queue with a dead-letter queue
D. A container orchestrator with persistent volumes

**B.** The pattern is an endpoint that routes to a stateless handler which persists to a managed table or document store.

title: Q2: Why do the Terraform fixtures use placeholder project names
body:
A. To make terraform apply succeed without a budget
B. To satisfy emulator authentication
C. To allow terraform plan without live state or credentials
D. To enable automatic provider upgrades

**C.** Placeholders keep the fixtures cost-free and offline; plan can resolve schema and references without contacting a provider.
